src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:119-139 and 243-256. information_schema is shared across all dialects. postgres maps to pg_catalog and the pg_ prefix. mysql maps to mysql, sys and performance_schema. sqlite maps to the sqlite_ and pragma_ prefixes. Any other dialect, or None, falls back to the union of all schemas and prefixes (_catalog_names, lines 134-137). is_catalog_table matches the schema in table.db and the prefix against the table name or table-function name, case-insensitively. In src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py, _source_expands_table (193-204) returns True (refuse) for any Scope whose expression, after unwrapping LATERAL, is not exp.Query/exp.Values (UNNEST, table-valued functions, parenthesized tables), and for any non-Scope source unless it is an exp.Table that is_catalog_table accepts. A function in FROM is a Table with an Anonymous this or a bare function node; the former is exempt only when readonly.is_catalog_table (readonly.py:243-256) matches its name or schema as a catalog, the latter always refused. So a star over a row-returning function is refused whatever it returns, except system catalog functions. For CTEs/subqueries, the star is checked in its own SELECT scope (_expands_table 172-190): with a Table source it is refused regardless of the outer query's column list, since the star scan covers the whole statement (155-160). Traced input: `SELECT a FROM (SELECT * FROM generate_series(1,3)) s` and `WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM t) SELECT id FROM c` are both refused. The only exemption is catalog tables, which the claim's catalog-function carve-out and the module docstring (21-22) acknowledge.

In whole_row.py, _whole_row_star (146-161) checks every exp.Star in the whole statement via find_all, not only the outer projection. Each non-exempt star is resolved by _expands_table (172-190) against the scope of its own nearest ancestor Select, so a star in a CTE or derived table SELECT list is evaluated at that inner SELECT. A CTE referenced only through another CTE is still checked, because traverse_scope scopes every CTE and the star walk is independent of references. The outer star over a Scope whose expression is a Query or Values is allowed (_source_expands_table, 193-202), which is safe because the inner stars were already checked. That exemption is documented separately at lines 14-15 (only a boolean leaves the subquery), so it is not a counterexample to the sentence. Set-operation branches are separate Selects with their own scopes and are checked. The remaining exemptions (COUNT, catalog tables) are listed in the same docstring.
